title: Exercise and Dementia ｜ 运动与失智症

sents.en: If this doesn't encourage you to squeeze in a workout today, nothing will: a new study from Sweden shows that women who were highly fit in mid-life were nearly 90% less likely to get dementia (失智) decades later.
sents.cn: 如果这都不能促使你今天挤出时间锻炼，那没什么能做到了：瑞典一项新研究表明，中年时身体素质极高的女性，几十年后患失智症（失智）的概率要低近90%。

sents.en: After initial exercise tests in middle age, researchers followed the women for 44 years.
sents.cn: 在中年进行初步运动测试后，研究人员对这些女性进行了44年的跟踪。

sents.en: Both groups lived just as long, but those who could ride an exercise bike at a fast rate for 6 minutes in the initial test had a much lower risk of dementia later on than those who couldn't complete the workout.
sents.cn: 两组人寿命一样长，但在初次测试中能以快速踩完6分钟健身车的女性，日后患失智症的风险远低于那些无法完成锻炼的女性。

sents.en: The study, published Wednesday in the journal Neurology, couldn't prove that exercise prevented dementia, and the findings aren't a surprise·it's long been known there's a correlation between exercise and decreased dementia risk·but the results were particularly dramatic.
sents.cn: 这项发表于周三《神经学》期刊的研究，无法证明运动能预防失智症，而且这一发现并不令人意外——人们早已知道运动与失智症风险降低之间存在关联——但结果却格外惊人。

sents.en: About 5% of the women with the highest peak workload·those who were able to bike the hardest over those 6 minutes·developed dementia, compared to 25% of those with medium fitness and 45% who weren't fit enough to finish the test, the study found.
sents.cn: 研究发现，在运动负荷最高（即那6分钟内踩得最卖力）的女性中，约5%患上了失智症；而在中等体能女性中这一比例为25%，体能不足以完成测试的女性则为45%。

sents.en: Overall, women who were highly fit compared to those who were moderately fit decreased their risk of dementia by 88%.
sents.cn: 总体而言，与中等体能女性相比，高体能女性患失智症的风险降低了88%。

sents.en: The few highly fit women who did develop dementia became symptomatic at age 90 on average, 11 years later than the moderately fit.
sents.cn: 少数确实患上失智症的高体能女性，平均在90岁时出现症状，比中等体能女性晚了11年。

sents.en: "I'm very surprised that the finding was so strong," said Ingmar Skoog, the paper's senior author and a psychiatry (精神病学) professor at The University of Gothenburg in Sweden.
sents.cn: "我非常惊讶这一发现如此有力，"该论文的资深作者、瑞典哥德堡大学精神病学（精神病学）教授英格马尔∙斯库格说。

sents.en: "It really shows the importance of exercise."
sents.cn: "它真正显示了运动的重要性。"

sents.en: Dementia, as defined in medical dictionaries, is a broad term that describes a loss of thinking ability, memory, attention, logical reasoning, and other mental abilities.
sents.cn: 正如医学词典所定义的，失智症是一个宽泛的术语，描述思考能力、记忆、注意力、逻辑推理及其他精神能力的丧失。

sents.en: These changes are severe enough to interfere with social or occupational functioning.
sents.cn: 这些变化严重到足以干扰社交或职业功能。

sents.en: Dementia isn't a disease. Instead, it's a group of symptoms caused by other conditions.
sents.cn: 失智症不是一种疾病，而是一组由其他状况引发的症状。

sents.en: It happens when the parts of your brain used for learning, memory, decision making, and language are damaged or diseased.
sents.cn: 当大脑中用于学习、记忆、决策和语言的部位受损或病变时，就会发生失智症。

sents.en: About 5%·8% of adults over age 65 have some form of dementia.
sents.cn: 约5%–8%的65岁以上成年人患有某种形式的失智症。

sents.en: This percentage doubles every 5 years after 65.
sents.cn: 这一比例在65岁后每5年翻一番。

sents.en: As many as half of people in their 80s have some dementia.
sents.cn: 多达一半的80多岁老人患有某种失智症。

sents.en: Dementia is not temporary confusion or forgetfulness that might result from an infection that heals without treatment.
sents.cn: 失智症并非感染未经治疗而自愈后可能产生的暂时性困惑或健忘。

sents.en: It can also come from an underlying (潜在的) illness or side effects of medications.
sents.cn: 它也可能来自潜在（潜在的）疾病或药物的副作用。

sents.en: Dementia typically gets worse over time.
sents.cn: 失智症通常会随时间恶化。

sents.en: People with dementia have problems with thinking and remembering that affect their ability to manage their daily life.
sents.cn: 失智症患者在思考和记忆方面存在问题，影响其打理日常生活的能力。

sents.en: Dementia is typically associated with declines in cognitive function.
sents.cn: 失智症通常与认知功能下降相关。

sents.en: Yet researchers have found an association between dementia and declines in hearing and other basic sensory functions.
sents.cn: 然而研究人员发现，失智症与听力和其它基本感官功能的退化之间也存在关联。

sents.en: Though the study mentioned above was fairly small(only 191 women took the initial fitness test, which means it's hard to maintain statistical significance while breaking the group down into sub-categories of more or less fit), it does give us hope that dementia can be prevented or delayed through exercise in one's middle age.
sents.cn: 尽管上述研究规模相当小（只有191名女性参加了初步体能测试，这意味着很难在将群体细分为体能较高或较低子类的同时保持统计显著性），但它确实给了我们希望：失智症可以通过中年时期的锻炼来预防或延缓。

sents.en: Alzheimer's (阿尔茨海默症) and other dementias are believed to begin 15–20 years before symptoms even appear, so it makes sense that exercising in mid-life would affect the risk, Skoog said.
sents.cn: 阿尔茨海默症（阿尔茨海默症）和其他失智症被认为在症状出现前15–20年就开始了，因此中年锻炼会影响风险，这说得通，斯库格说。

sents.en: Exercise alone is not likely to prevent Alzheimer's, but the study shows people are not helpless in the face of one of the most feared, costliest and common diseases of old age, he added.
sents.cn: 单靠运动不太可能预防阿尔茨海默症，但他补充道，研究表明，面对这种最令人恐惧、最昂贵也最常见的老年疾病之一，人们并非无能为力。

sents.en: And the same activities that help prevent Alzheimer's· including avoiding smoking, getting adequate exercise and sleep and eating a healthy diet ·also prevent heart disease, he said, making them even more worthwhile.
sents.cn: 他说，那些有助于预防阿尔茨海默症的活动——包括戒烟、充足运动与睡眠、健康饮食——也能预防心脏病，这让它们更值得去做。

sents.en: "You can do something yourself to decrease your odds," Skoog said.
sents.cn: "你可以自己做一些事来降低几率，"斯库格说。

sents.en: Maintaining a healthy lifestyle in mid-life, decades before disease sets in, makes sense, said David Knopman, a fellow of the American Academy of Neurology, who was not involved in the study.
sents.cn: 在疾病发生前几十年的中年期就保持健康的生活方式，是明智的，美国神经病学学会会员、未参与该研究的戴维∙克诺普曼说。

sents.en: "I suspect it's a dose," said Knopman, also associate director of the Alzheimer's Disease Research Center at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota.
sents.cn: "我怀疑这是一种剂量效应，"克诺普曼说，他也是明尼苏达州罗切斯特市梅奥诊所阿尔茨海默病研究中心的副主任。

sents.en: "Starting in late life is better than not starting at all, but starting in mid-life seems to offer a larger benefit."
sents.cn: "晚年才开始比根本不开始要好，但中年就开始似乎能带来更大的益处。"

sents.en: Although it is not entirely clear why exercise helps put off or prevent Alzheimer's, Knopman said it's likely that exercise maintains good blood flow to the brain.
sents.cn: 尽管尚不完全清楚运动为何有助于推迟或预防阿尔茨海默症，克诺普曼说，运动很可能维持了大脑良好的血液供应。

sents.en: "When the brain is healthier from a vascular (血管的) point of view, it can absorb more Alzheimer's pathogen (病原体) before people become symptomatic," he said.
sents.cn: "从血管（血管的）角度看，当大脑更健康时，在人们出现症状前就能吸收更多的阿尔茨海默病原（病原体），"他说。

sents.en: The message isn't that everyone needs to run marathons in middle age, Knopman said, but a healthy lifestyle pays off.
sents.cn: 克诺普曼说，这话的意思并不是人人都需要在中年跑马拉松，而是健康的生活方式会有回报。

sents.en: This type of study can't say exactly what kind of exercise is best, or how much is needed—only a study that has a placebo (安慰剂) group and tracks people going forward can do that, said Keith Fargo, director of scientific programs and outreach at the non-profit Alzheimer's Association.
sents.cn: 这类研究无法确切说明哪种运动最好，或需要多少运动量——只有设了安慰剂（安慰剂）组并向前跟踪受试者的研究才能做到这一点，非营利组织阿尔茨海默协会科学项目与外联主任基思∙法戈说。

sents.en: "The literature has not yet settled on an amount or type of exercise that is going to be key, although the bulk of literature has suggested that aerobic (有氧的) exercise is what you need to be doing," he said.
sents.cn: "文献尚未就关键的运动量或运动类型达成共识，尽管大量文献表明你需要做的是有氧（有氧的）运动，"他说。

sents.en: That doesn't mean you have to compete in marathons but "more than a 10-min dog walk" would be a good idea, Fargo said.
sents.cn: 这并不意味着你必须参加马拉松，但"比遛狗走10分钟再多一点"会是个好主意，法戈说。

sents.en: Several lifestyle studies are getting underway soon, including one backed by the Alzheimer's Association called the US POINTER study, which will offer at-risk adults, ages 60–79, a series of lifestyle interventions (干预) to see if they impact Alzheimer's risk.
sents.cn: 几项生活方式研究即将展开，包括一项由阿尔茨海默协会支持的名为USPOINTER的研究，它将为60–79岁的高风险成年人提供一系列生活方式干预（干预），以观察它们是否影响阿尔茨海默症风险。

sents.en: That and other Alzheimer's-related studies are always looking for volunteers to participate, he said.
sents.cn: 他说，这项研究及其他阿尔茨海默相关研究一直在寻找志愿者参与。

sents.en: O) In the next three to five years, these studies should allow researchers to provide clearer recommendations for exercise and other lifestyle modifications that might reduce Alzheimer's risk, such as sleep, diet and social activities, Fargo said.
sents.cn: O）在未来三到五年内，这些研究应能让研究人员就运动及其他可能降低阿尔茨海默症风险的生活方式改变（如睡眠、饮食和社交活动）提供更为明确的建议，法戈说。

sents.en: But it's already quite clear that exercising at any point in life is better for your brain than not exercising at all, Fargo added.
sents.cn: 但他补充道，有一点已经相当清楚：人生中任何阶段运动都比完全不运动对大脑更好。

sents.en: P) "If you don't want to have dementia when you're 80, the time to start getting fit is now," he said.
sents.cn: P）"如果你不想在80岁时患上失智症，开始健身的时候就是现在，"他说。

sents.en: "It may not necessarily give you a longer life, but there's a compelling body of work that it will give you more good years."
sents.cn: "这未必能让你长寿，但大量有力的研究证明，它会让你拥有更多健康的岁月。"
